summary: Serverless architecture: React Native with Expo with Supabase Cloud and Supabase Postgres on Supabase platform in ap-south-1. Driven mainly by team.has_devops and team.size; about $25-90/month.

architecture.justification: No devops engineer, a team of 2 and spiky traffic suit pay-per-use serverless or backend-as-a-service, which scales to zero between peaks.

alternatives.why_not: Needs 12+ people, a devops engineer, 1,000,000+ users and scalability priority 4+; here team.size is 2, team.has_devops is false, scale.users_12_months is 2,000, priorities.scalability is 2.
No workload is heavy enough to need its own service (realtime under 2,000 concurrent users, no model training, no write-heavy iot, analytics or gaming).

frontend.justification: React Native with Expo: supports an on-device store for offline use; written in javascript, which the team already uses; quick to build with for a 10-week MVP; low operations burden for a team of 2 with no devops engineer. One TypeScript codebase for Android and iOS.

alternatives.why_not: Native Android (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose): none of the team's languages (javascript, python) is used by Native Android (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose).
Ionic with Capacitor scores lower on maintainability (3.4 against 4.4, priorities.maintainability is 4), which accounts for 3.8 of the 9.0-point gap.

tradeoffs: Native modules still need native knowledge occasionally
Heavier than native; keep the bundle lean for 2 GB devices.

backend.justification: Supabase Cloud: fits a serverless architecture with no servers to run; includes sign-in, file storage out of the box, so fewer services for a team of 2 to wire up; javascript like the frontend, so a team of 2 works in one language; quick to build with for a 10-week MVP; low operations burden for a team of 2 with no devops engineer. Postgres, Auth, Storage, Realtime and Edge Functions behind one dashboard. Deployed in ap-south-1.

alternatives.why_not: Azure Functions (Flex Consumption) scores 1.5 points higher on its own, but the best full stack built around it totals 13.8 points less once hosting, database and cloud fit are counted.
AWS Lambda + Amazon API Gateway scores 2.1 points higher on its own, but the best full stack built around it totals 14.6 points less once hosting, database and cloud fit are counted.
Excluded: Firebase (Blaze plan) processes user data in US, which breaks data_residency=india.

tradeoffs: Hosted free projects pause after inactivity
Complex server logic ends up in edge functions or database functions

database.justification: Supabase Postgres: bundled with Supabase; a relational database suits the data: the input has no key-value, document or very-high-scale signal; location queries are supported (PostGIS); about $12-16 a month for this layer against the $100 monthly budget; low operations burden for a team of 2 with no devops engineer. ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Deployed in ap-south-1.

alternatives.why_not: Azure SQL Database scores lower on cost (2.0 against 5.0, priorities.cost is 5), which accounts for 14.2 of the 25.4-point gap.
Amazon RDS for MySQL scores lower on cost (0.9 against 5.0, priorities.cost is 5), which accounts for 19.3 of the 31.6-point gap.

tradeoffs: Vertical scaling first; sharding needs extra tooling
Self-managed HA and backups take skill

hosting.justification: Supabase platform: free at the expected load; quick to build with for a 10-week MVP. Hosts the Supabase backend. Deployed in ap-south-1.

alternatives.why_not: Azure Functions (Flex Consumption) scores 4.0 points higher on its own, but the best full stack built around it totals 13.8 points less once hosting, database and cloud fit are counted.
AWS Lambda + Amazon API Gateway scores 4.6 points higher on its own, but the best full stack built around it totals 14.6 points less once hosting, database and cloud fit are counted.

tradeoffs: Does not host arbitrary backend frameworks

supporting.justification: Supabase Auth + MSG91 OTP: already included with Supabase; registered for Indian DLT SMS rules; same vendor (Supabase) as the core stack, so one account and no cross-vendor traffic; about $3-16 a month for this layer against the $100 monthly budget; quick to build with for a 10-week MVP. Email, phone OTP, social and SSO bundled with the Supabase database. Deployed in ap-south-1.

supporting.choice: SQLite local store with outbox sync
supporting.justification: SQLite local store with outbox sync: on-device SQLite with a sync queue fits the mobile framework; free at the expected load; quick to build with for a 10-week MVP. Simple offline-first pattern: write locally, replay to your API when online.

alternatives.why_not: SQLite local store with outbox sync is preferred because on-device SQLite with a sync queue fits the mobile framework.
WatermelonDB: operations burden 5 of 5 with no devops engineer.
Excluded: needs Firestore as the database.

tradeoffs: You design conflict handling

assumptions: Priced for 2,000 monthly active users (the larger of users_at_launch and users_12_months), interpolated between list-price anchors in the knowledge base.
Prices are list prices of the cheapest region inside the chosen residency zone; taxes are excluded.
Database storage is priced for 100 GB (scale.data_volume_gb_12_months).
The upper bound includes a x1.25 allowance for spiky traffic (not stacked on the staging allowance).
The upper bound is limited to 3 times the lower bound: the components do not all peak in the same month, so the band stays within one order of magnitude.
Supabase Postgres: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase platform: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase Auth: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase Storage: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
Supabase Queues (pgmq) and pg_cron: included in the Supabase Cloud price, with no separate charge
GitHub Actions: free tier used at the low end (Free: 2,000 minutes per month on private repos; unlimited on public)
Sentry: free tier used at the low end (Developer plan free: 5K errors per month)
Payment gateway fees (about 2% per transaction), one-time costs, domain names and developer seats are not infrastructure and are excluded.

warnings.message: Sentry has no india region; log only scrubbed events and keep personal data out of telemetry.
CERT-In Directions (28 April 2022) require system logs to be kept for 180 days within India and cyber incidents to be reported within 6 hours; set log retention in the India region accordingly.
India DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025: Notice and consent for processing personal data; Data principal rights: access, correction, erasure, grievance redressal. The stack keeps data in ap-south-1.

The low end of the estimate relies on free tiers: GitHub Actions (Free: 2,000 minutes per month on private repos; unlimited on public); Sentry (Developer plan free: 5K errors per month). Check them against the expected traffic.
The app records location, which is personal data: ask for consent before collecting it, store only the precision the feature needs and set a retention period.
Target devices have about 2 GB of RAM: keep the app bundle small, use the Hermes engine for React Native, paginate lists and avoid holding images in memory.
SMS to Indian numbers must go through a DLT-registered sender and templates; register before launch.
